verses.t: The Watchers and the birth of the giants

These are the words that remain of the Book of Giants, recovered in Aramaic fragments among the scrolls of Qumran, with kindred memories in the later Manichaean Book of Giants. The work does not survive whole. What follows is an original English rendering of the story the fragments preserve — not a copy of any modern copyrighted edition.

In the days when the Watchers came down to the earth, they took wives from among the daughters of men, and the women bore them sons. The sons were giants, and the giants begot Nephilim, and the Nephilim were upon the earth in those days.

They became great in stature and in appetite. They devoured the labour of men, and when men could no longer sustain them they turned their hands against the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and creeping things, and at last against one another.
Violence filled the earth. The cry of flesh went up before the Holy One, and the earth itself accused them.

verses.t: The dreams of the giants
Then two among the giants, Ohya and Hahya, sons of Shemihazah, were troubled in the night. They dreamed, and their dreams were alike in terror.

In one vision a tablet was thrown into the water, and when it was taken up, only a third of it remained. In another, a garden was full of trees; gardeners came and watered it; then fire and water destroyed all the trees but one.
The giants did not understand. Fear entered them, for they perceived that a judgment was prepared, and that their own end was written.
They sought an interpreter who still walked with God.

verses.t: Mahaway is sent to Enoch

They chose Mahaway, son of Barakel, for his father was of the Watchers, and Mahaway knew the wilderness and the ends of the earth. They said to him: Go to Enoch the scribe, the distinguished scribe, and carry our dreams before him. Ask him to interpret them, and to make known what will befall us.
Mahaway lifted himself as upon wings of the wind. He crossed the wilderness, and the regions of death, and he came to the place where Enoch dwelt, far from the dwellings of men.
He bowed and said: The giants have sent me, my lord. Two dreams have shaken them. They ask of you a writing, that they may know whether there is hope, or whether the end is decreed.

verses.t: Enoch the scribe answers
Enoch the scribe heard him, and he was grieved for the earth, and for the children who had been born of the mixing of heaven and flesh. He took tablets and wrote.
He said: Go, Mahaway, and say to the giants and to the Watchers who begot them: You have corrupted the earth. You have done what was not appointed to you. The cry of blood has reached the Holy One.
Look, a deluge is prepared, and fire, and the days of your might shall be cut short. A remnant of flesh shall be kept, and the earth shall be cleansed.

Yet the interpretation of the tablet that was broken, and of the trees that perished, is this: destruction is decreed upon you; but the one tree that remains is a sign that the Holy One will not make an end of all life.

verses.t: The tablet is read
Mahaway returned. The giants assembled, and the Watchers with them, and the writing of Enoch was read in their hearing.
Some among them raged. Ohya lifted his voice against the judgment, and he boasted of strength, saying that none could stand before the giants.
Others trembled. They understood that their own dreams had already spoken what Enoch wrote. They argued one with another, and there was no peace in their camp.

verses.t: Gilgamesh and Hobabish
Among the names the fragments still keep are Gilgamesh and Hobabish. They stand in the assembly of the giants as mighty ones of old, men of name.
Gilgamesh spoke of his own strength, and of the weakness of flesh before death. Hobabish was counted among those whose power had made the earth afraid.
The book remembers them not as heroes to be praised, but as witnesses that even the famous are gathered to the judgment that was written.

verses.t: The quarrel of the giants
Ohya said to his companions: I have been near the Holy One in my dream, and I have seen that we shall not be held guiltless.
Then he turned and strove with his brother, and the giants divided. Some sought to petition for mercy; some sought to make war upon heaven itself.
Their counsel came to nothing. For the sentence was not in their hands, and the earth was already appointed for washing.

verses.t: The sentence of the Watchers

Concerning the Watchers who came down, the writing of Enoch was hard. They had left the heaven of their appointment. They had taught what was not given them to teach. They had taken wives, and the mixing was violence.
They shall be bound, said the scribe, until the day of the great judgment. Their children shall fall by the sword, and by the waters, and by their own hands.
And the earth shall rest, and be clean of the corruption that was done upon it.

verses.t: A remnant is spoken
Yet in the broken tablet a third remained, and in the garden one tree was not cut down. The fragments keep this mercy beside the wrath.
A seed of men shall be preserved. Knowledge of the Holy One shall not perish from the earth. After the waters, life shall begin again.
So the giants heard, and their greatness did not deliver them. The book that named them is itself broken, as the tablet in the dream was broken, and only pieces remain.

verses.t: What is lost
The rest of the Book of Giants has not come down to us. Columns are missing. Names are half-erased. The Manichaean version, written many centuries later, retells kindred episodes in another tongue.
We read what the wilderness kept, and we leave the gaps as gaps. The Watchers, the dreams, the journey of Mahaway, the tablets of Enoch, the names of the mighty — these the fragments still speak.
And they agree with the Book of Enoch in this: that the earth was filled with violence, and that a judgment was set, and that a remnant was remembered.
